articles.title: EVgo opens its first Tesla Superchargers, with hundreds more planned
articles.summary: EVgo opened a 12-stall Supercharger in a Chicago grocery-store lot, with Magic Dock plugs so both NACS and CCS cars can charge without a personal adapter. It is the first of hundreds of stalls the company plans to add, which gives drivers who cannot charge at home another fast-charging option that shows up in Tesla navigation.

articles.title: Major EV charging rollout underway at 254-apartment building in Canberra
articles.summary: Nox Energy is fitting a 254-apartment building in Canberra with shared charging infrastructure, and more than 90 residents have already paid to add a smart socket at their own parking space. The install is part of an ARENA-backed program that aims to put nearly 2,000 of those sockets in apartment buildings, so residents can plug in without a building-wide electrical rebuild.

articles.title: Pennsylvania is way ahead on NEVI charging, with another $37 million for public ports
articles.summary: Pennsylvania is putting $37 million in federal NEVI funding toward 515 new public charging ports in the Philadelphia region, including 157 on-street Level 2 ports from It's Electric and 62 more curbside ports from Voltpost. Those are the plugs that matter for drivers without a driveway, though construction is still ahead and they are not open yet.

articles.title: State of Walmart EV Charging: November 2026 Update
articles.summary: Walmart's fast-charging network reached 132 sites and 1,108 stalls by the end of October, and every 400 kW charger has both a CCS1 plug and a NACS plug. Average pricing is about $0.47 per kWh on peak and $0.29 off peak, a useful benchmark for drivers who have to fast-charge because they cannot plug in at home.

articles.title: Thousands of public EV chargers are coming, but they could be unusable
articles.summary: Australia's Accelerating EV Charging Program is set to put about 14,000 chargers on power poles in dense neighborhoods where residents lack off-street parking, with the first installs expected from March 2027. Installers are not required to get EV-only parking, and chargers without a dedicated bay are often blocked by gas cars, so a pole on your street is not the same as a guaranteed overnight spot.

articles.title: NSW apartment owners get a right to install an EV charger, but not yet
articles.summary: NSW has passed a law that will stop a strata committee from unreasonably blocking an owner who wants an EV charger on their own apartment lot, including when the work touches common property. The charging rules are signed into law but not in force until an official start date is set, and a renter still needs the apartment owner to make the request.
